title: New EU rules to help local authorities tackle the housing crisis
content: New EU rules have been proposed to support EU countries and cities address the affordable housing crisis, particularly housing used for purposes other than primary residence. The rules give public authorities the legal certainty when they choose to act, based on local specificities, within EU law.

title: The EU’s plan to grow innovation in Europe
content: The Commission has proposed a new European innovation act to help Europe's most innovative ideas be developed, financed and scaled up in Europe. The proposal will help innovative companies access financing and establish a common approach for research and development procurement.

title: EU and Greenland: €200 million to strengthen our partnership and engagement
content: On her visit to Nuuk, the President of the European Commission Ursula von der Leyen announced that €200 million will be invested in and with Greenland this year and the next. The EU, Greenland and Denmark have also reinforced their partnership with a new Joint Declaration.

title: Europol supports bust of major Western Mediterranean smuggling network
content: Europol supported a Spanish-led investigation that dismantled one of the largest criminal networks smuggling cannabis, synthetic drugs, migrants, weapons, and fugitives across the Western Mediterranean. The operation led to the arrest of 78 suspects and the seizure of 18 high-speed vessels.

title: Six of the world’s 16 major emitters reduced their emissions in 2025
content: Although greenhouse gas emissions reached a record high in 2025, six of the 16 major emitters, contributing over 1% of global emissions, achieved reductions, including Australia, Brazil and Japan. The EU cut its greenhouse gas emissions by 0.2% relative to 2024, while US emissions rose by +2.2%.

title: EU sends more aid to Nepal to care for flood survivors
content: As families across Nepal face the human toll of its recent deadly floods, the EU is adding to the relief effort by delivering 82 tonnes of essential supplies, including nutrition and shelter. This comes in addition to the EU’s ongoing response. A further €500,000 will facilitate EU aid delivery.

title: Science on the go: 10 EU-funded podcasts, from AI to climate change
content: Are you curious about science? Give these 10 podcasts by EU-funded researchers a listen to expand your knowledge about research into AI, climate change, food fraud and citizen science, among others. This autumn, why not learn something new, whether at home, in the office or on your commute.

title: EU allocates €2 million in humanitarian aid to support flash flood victims in Nepal
content: In response to the massive flash flood that has caused over 300 deaths in Nepal, the EU has allocated €2 million in humanitarian aid to support affected communities. This emergency funding will help address immediate needs including food, healthcare, clean water and sanitation.

title: EU further extends support to Serbia as wildfires intensify
content: As wildfires continue and strong winds are forecast in affected areas, EU firefighting support to Serbia has been extended until 5 September. Four helicopters from the rescEU strategic reserve from Czechia, Romania and Slovakia and a ground firefighting team from Romania will remain deployed.

title: EU reaffirms solidarity with Ukraine on 35th anniversary of regained independence
content: On 24 August, we celebrate Ukraine’s Independence Day. This occasion embodies the bravery, resistance and resilience of the Ukrainian people in the face of Russia’s vicious war of aggression. To mark the occasion, the EU Commission unfurled the Ukraine flag in front of the Berlaymont building.

title: World humanitarian day: EU answering to growing global humanitarian needs
content: August 19 marks World Humanitarian Day, an opportunity to celebrate the indispensable and tireless life-saving efforts of aid workers worldwide. Find out how the EU helps to protect local aid workers around the globe and makes sure humanitarian aid is delivered fast and effectively to those in need.

title: EU supports Belgium and Spain as wildfires spread
content: As wildfires spread around Europe, the EU has mobilised support to Belgium and Spain. Planes and helicopters have been dispatched to support local firefighters battling the blaze in the Hautes Fagnes, Belgium, and more than 100 ground firefighters are assisting firefighters in Spain’s Aragon region.

title: How EU research can help respond to heatwaves
content: With climate change, Europe is getting warmer and heatwaves are becoming more frequent and intense. While the immediate focus is on responding to the emergencies, EU-funded research develops the knowledge and solutions needed to strengthen society’s resilience.

title: How to further protect victims' rights: Submit ideas by 5 November
content: The European Commission launched an open public consultation to gather feedback for its new EU Strategy on victims’ rights. Victims of crime, citizens as well as all relevant actors in the field are invited to contribute. You can submit your contribution until 5 November 2026.

title: New packaging rules for less waste and easier recycling
content: Today, new rules on packaging start to apply in the EU. They address the environmental challenges caused by packaging waste, harmonise rules for businesses across the single market, and create opportunities for businesses involved in recycling and sustainable packaging solutions.

title: European Health Insurance Card: keeping you safe while travelling abroad
content: You can use the European Health Insurance Card for necessary or urgent medical care when travelling abroad, under the same conditions and at the same cost as people insured in that country. It’s valid in any EU country, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, Switzerland, and the United Kingdom. Read more.

title: New rules on AI transparency start applying
content: On 2 August 2026, new rules on the transparency of AI systems take effect. They will help people recognise when they are interacting with AI or are exposed to AI-generated content, so they can make informed decisions and better protect themselves from misinformation or deception.

title: EU launches AI Gigafactories call
content: The EU has launched a call for tenders to establish up to seven AI Gigafactories across Europe. The initiative will expand Europe's AI computing capacity and give all relevant actors access to infrastructure for training, inference and fine-tuning advanced frontier AI models.

content: The European Commission is preparing a new set of policy initiatives on school education. title: Right to repair: New consumer rights for easy and attractive repairs
content: The Directive on repair of goods became national law across EU countries on 31 July 2026. The new rules will help create a system that favours repairing a product over purchasing a new one. They will help consumers save, boost the circular economy and support sustainable consumption.

title: Know your EU passenger rights before you travel
content: If you’re heading off on a summer break soon, rest assured that the EU has you covered if your travel plans run into trouble. Whether your flight is cancelled, your train delayed or your luggage lost aboard your cruise ship, you have the right to make a claim under EU-wide passenger rights.

title: Frontex co-led operation seizes nearly half a tonne of cocaine off European shores
content: Nearly half a tonne of cocaine, dropped in open water for small boats to scoop up before it reached European shores, has been seized in a sea operation co-led by Frontex. Some 14 countries spent a month targeting drug traffickers at sea before seizing the 454 kg of cocaine and arresting 5 suspects.

title: Wildfires: EU sends planes and firefighters to France and Spain
content: The EU has deployed assistance to both France and Spain as ongoing wildfires have displaced more than 300,000 people. It has sent several planes and helicopters to France as well as planes, personnel and vehicles to Spain. The EU's Copernicus satellite service is providing rapid emergency maps.

title: Cast your vote on new euro banknote design proposals
content: Have your say on the ten shortlisted design proposals for the next series of euro banknotes that have been unveiled by the European Central Bank. An online survey where you can give your feedback is open until 21 September. The winning proposal will be selected around the end of the year.

title: New EU energy rules: cleaner, more secure energy and stronger consumer protection
content: New electricity and gas market rules are taking effect across the EU. They aim to make Europe’s energy system cleaner, more secure and resilient. They protect citizens from energy price spikes and give them stronger rights and control over their energy choices.

title: Google fined for breaching Digital Markets Act
content: The Commission found that Google had breached the DMA by favouring its own services in Google Search and by imposing restrictions preventing businesses from directing consumers to alternative, often lower-cost, purchasing channels on Google Play. The Commission imposed total fines of €890 million.

title: A renewed commitment to protect and empower the EU's citizens
content: The European Pillar of Social Rights helps to improve people's lives through better jobs, equal opportunities, quality working conditions and strong social protection. A communication has been published that looks at its impact and highlights three areas which require urgent additional attention.

title: A plan to make Europe the first electro-continent
content: The Commission has put forward the electrification action plan as part of the EU’s wider efforts to boost Europe’s competitiveness, decarbonisation and independence. The plan introduces measures to make electricity more competitive and to incentivise the use of electricity-based technologies.
